llm.summary: This booking skill is coherent, but it can place or change real phone reservations through an external service without clearly requiring user confirmation for high-impact actions.

dimensions.detail: Use of LIFECLAW_API_TOKEN and network requests to the LifeClaw API is disclosed and proportionate to the service, but it transmits names, phone numbers, party size, special requests, and reservation details externally.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The artifact contains Markdown instructions and API documentation only; no executable install scripts, local dependencies, hooks, or hidden setup behavior were found.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The trigger text is broad, including generic words like find, book, reserve, cancel, and reschedule, while the workflow does not explicitly require final user confirmation before phone calls, cancellations, reschedules, or booking-record updates.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No local persistence or privilege escalation is present. The service retains booking records accessible to the token owner and exposes booking history, balance, and record update endpoints.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose matches the main capabilities: business search, details lookup, AI phone booking, inquiries, cancellation, and rescheduling. These are real-world actions involving personal booking data and merchant calls.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review before installing. Only use this skill when you intentionally want an external service to search businesses or call a merchant for you. Confirm all booking, cancellation, reschedule, contact, and language details before allowing a phone call or record update, and keep the LIFECLAW_API_TOKEN scoped and revocable.
llm.findings:
[SQP-1] unexpected: The broad invocation wording is materially concerning because the skill can initiate external calls and reservation changes; this finding is supported by the artifact.
[SQP-3] expected: Automatic merchant-language matching is disclosed and purpose-related, but there is no documented user override, so it adds risk for calls made on the user's behalf.
[E1] expected: External transmission of booking and contact data is core to the skill and is disclosed in the privacy section, so this is expected but still important for user consent.
[SDI-1] expected: Balance, pricing, and top-up documentation are adjacent to paid API use and disclosed in the reference; this does not by itself indicate hidden wallet control.
